scope: human-only temporal observability plus non-executable FeCO wiring evidence

direct_functional_connectome_evidence.claim: FeCO claw and hook axons connect to local VNC interneurons and leg motor neurons, supporting fast local proprioceptive feedback pathways.

Hook flexion and hook extension axons have strongly different postsynaptic connectivity; same-direction claw and hook populations share more downstream connectivity than opposite-direction hook populations.
Hook axons receive substantial inhibitory presynaptic input, prominently from 9A neurons, consistent with context-dependent suppression of expected proprioceptive feedback.

Flexion-tuned claw and hook axons provide net excitatory feedback toward tibia extensor motor output and inhibitory feedback toward tibia flexor motor output; extension-tuned populations show the complementary pattern.

malecns_systematic_context.claim: MaleCNS systematic annotation treats SNpp39 and SNpp41 as proprioceptive leg sensory types associated with FeCO hook circuitry.
MaleCNS connectivity groups SNpp39 and SNpp41 with proprioceptive types receiving strong connectivity from inhibitory hemilineage 09A.

polarity_boundary.promotion_rule: Do not bind engineering hook_extension/hook_flexion channels to SNpp39/SNpp41 until direct type-level physiology or an independently validated immutable identity crosswalk is available.

research_interpretation: Temporal receptor traces can be compared with known directional FeCO circuit motifs for human analysis only.
Temporal coincidence or anti-correlation is not identity evidence and cannot resolve SNpp39/SNpp41 polarity.
Connectome pathway sign and motor-module targeting may strengthen a physiology-supported hypothesis but cannot substitute for a direct systematic-type tuning crosswalk.
